prompts.title: Domains list
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE crisp high-fidelity screenshot-style UI concept for Tabernacle, a compact Firefox browser sidebar. The supplied image is a STYLE AND LAYOUT REFERENCE of the actual existing domain-filter interface, not content to reproduce exactly. Match its system sans-serif typography, flat white surfaces, charcoal text #242424, fine grey dividers, quiet grey secondary text, small restrained rounded corners, compact utilitarian proportions. This is a new design proposal.
Composition: portrait image approximately 960 by 1600 pixels. Show one straight-on sidebar representing 360 CSS pixels wide by 600 CSS pixels tall, filling almost the whole image, with only a narrow light grey 12px outer gutter and a thin grey outline. No device frame, perspective, shadows, branding title outside the app, explanatory captions or arrows. UI text must be crisp and legible. Preserve compact density, with adequate whitespace beneath short lists.
The normal tree, search capsule, folder breadcrumbs and pinned-tabs strip are COMPLETELY REPLACED by this dedicated view. Do not show them.
Bottom toolbar always fixed at bottom, white with a fine top divider. EXACTLY SIX evenly spaced outline icon buttons in this order: plus (new tab), folder-plus (new folder), opposing vertical chevrons (fold, visibly disabled pale grey), globe (Domains, SELECTED with pale grey-lavender rounded-square background), recent-history counterclockwise clock, settings gear. The new globe icon is a familiar wireframe world with longitude and latitude strokes, NOT a spiderweb or internet browser logo. Keep all six controls and ample click targets. No footer text labels.
Avoid cards, gradients, giant typography, bright accent buttons, extra navigation, diagrams, fabricated product branding, side menus or duplicate domains. These are ordinary open-tab counts, never notifications.
State 1: default Domains list, no domains pinned yet.
Replace the reference site's orange-tinted header with a very gently tinted neutral grey header approximately 76 CSS pixels tall. In one row: large charcoal outline globe at left, heading EXACTLY "Domains" in 22px semibold, large X close button at far right returning to the normal tree. No subtitle in the header.
Below: a compact 32px-high toolbar showing "9 domains" at left and "Most tabs" at right with a small descending-sort icon; this is a quiet fixed sort label, not a prominent button.
Below that are nine flat compact 40px-high rows. Each row has a small recognisable site favicon at left, exact domain text in regular 14px, a right-aligned grey numeric tab count, and a small OUTLINE pushpin button at far right. All pin buttons are visible but subtle. Use these EXACT nine rows in EXACT order and keep these counts associated correctly:
youtube.com | 18
github.com | 12
reddit.com | 9
en.wikipedia.org | 7
figma.com | 6
bbc.co.uk | 5
stackoverflow.com | 4
news.ycombinator.com | 3
developer.mozilla.org | 2
Use recognisable compact favicons: red YouTube play, GitHub cat silhouette, orange Reddit, black Wikipedia W, Figma shapes, black BBC, orange Stack Overflow, orange Hacker News Y, dark MDN mark.
One quiet helper line below the list reads EXACTLY "Domains with 2 or more tabs". Do not show a Pinned section in this no-pins state. Do not include any row with one or zero tabs. No selected domain row; all rows white. The globe footer button is clearly selected. The only X is in the header, not on domain rows. No chevrons on domain rows.

State 3: user clicked the pinned news.ycombinator.com row and sees the existing domain-filter page, with a compact way back to the Domains list.
Keep the actual supplied screenshot's domain-header style and content: very pale warm orange full-width header approximately 76 CSS pixels tall. Large orange square Hacker News favicon with white Y at left, bold dark heading EXACTLY "Hacker News", and smaller grey domain EXACTLY "news.ycombinator.com" directly below it; large X close button far right. X exits to the normal tree.

"Show HN: A little tool for organising browser tabs | Hacker News"
"A quieter way to browse the web | Hacker News"
"Hacker News"

Keep substantial blank white list space beneath these three tabs. Footer has EXACTLY the SAME SIX icons as described, including the SELECTED globe to communicate that the user is still browsing by domain. No domain directory mixed into these tab results, no thumbnails, video players, row counts or extra sidebar controls.
